evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep jumps straight into availability check without framing time box or dependable quote promise: 'Yeah, we actually do have available on October 1st.'
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Never asked. Rep moves directly into logistics probing after initial availability confirmation.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Rep gives hourly rate ($204/hour for two movers) but does not anchor to a typical range for a 2,400 sq ft home or personalize beyond the rate itself. Customer initiates estimate discussion ('I'm thinking $6,700 somewhere') and rep partially corrects upward mentioning 'five to seven hours' for 'three bedroom apartment,' but this is reactive, not proactively anchored.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Not asked. Rep states the rate and moves on without asking if it feels fair or pausing for customer reaction.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Never asked. Call ends with customer saying 'I'll probably give you a call back once I determine' and rep saying 'Sounds good. Thank you bye-bye.' Rep never asks 'Would you like our help with your move?' or equivalent explicit close.

top_strength: Jules gathered all four discovery basics (name/address, move date, route, size) cleanly and efficiently in Section 1, establishing a clear starting point for the estimate.
coaching_note: You skipped the entire opening value frame (no 10–15 minute time-box or dependable quote promise), never asked about concerns or agenda, gave no anchored range estimate, and ended without an explicit ask for the business — this read as a partial inquiry call, not a full sales call. Return to the script: open with your quid pro quo, probe Their Concerns deeply, anchor and personalize your estimate, and close with a direct 'Would you like our help?'
